key_insight: Applying orthogonal gradient projection inside a shared LoRA adapter disentangles conflicting task gradients so each task keeps its useful update directions while removing interference, preserving parameter-efficiency with large gains in per-task performance.
problem_solved: Negative transfer in multi-task LoRA: sharing a single low-rank adapter across tasks causes conflicting gradient updates that degrade individual task performance compared to single-task fine-tuning.
method: Detect gradient conflict directions between tasks in the shared LoRA parameter space.
Project each task's gradient onto the subspace orthogonal to identified conflicting components (Orthogonal Gradient Projection) to remove interference while retaining task-aligned updates.
Integrate orthogonal projection into the LoRA update loop with minimal computational and storage overhead to keep a single shared adapter.
impact: Enables robust, parameter-efficient multi-task adaptation of LLMs by reducing negative transfer—practitioners can deploy one shared LoRA adapter with near single-task performance across tasks, saving storage and maintenance cost.
visual_elements: Gradient-vector diagram showing two conflicting task gradients and the orthogonal projection that removes the interfering component.
Schematic of a shared LoRA adapter decomposed into preserved task-aligned directions vs. removed conflict directions.
Bar chart comparing per-task accuracy (single-task FT vs. vanilla multi-task LoRA vs. OGP-LoRA) to illustrate reduced negative transfer.
Training flowchart highlighting where Orthogonal Gradient Projection is applied in the LoRA update loop.
paper_title: Disentangling Task Conflicts in Multi-Task LoRA via Orthogonal Gradient Projection
paper_authors: Ziyu Yang, Guibin Chen, Yuxin Yang, Aoxiong Zeng, Xiangquan Yang
